title: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating cancer cells (CTC), and biomarker evaluation of Nectin4, Trop2, and Her2neu in patients with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) prior to robotic-assisted radical cystectomy.
summary:
Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is often treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) before radical resection of the bladder (RARC). In this study, we are investigating whether circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) and circulating tumour cells (CTCs) in patients' blood can be used as biomarkers to better assess disease progression and treatment response. In addition, we are analysing certain biomarkers (Nectin4, Trop2, Her2neu) that may play a role in cancer biology and therapy response.

The study includes 50 patients with MIBC receiving NAC. Blood and urine samples will be taken before, during and after therapy and analysed using state-of-the-art molecular biology methods. The aim is to gain new insights into the effectiveness of the therapy and possible personalised treatment approaches.

interventions.name: Evaluation of the prognostic and predicitve value of ctDNA, CTC, and Nectin-4, Trop2, and Her2neu in patients with MIBC receiving NAC.
